examples.en: The president released a statement yesterday.
The statement contains the government's position.
The prime minister's statement was broadcast.
I read the full text of the statement in the newspaper.
Opinions were divided over the content of the statement.
We had a class on writing statements at school.

explain: 정부나 기관이 공식 입장을 알리려고 낸 글을 말하고, 주로 뉴스에서 '담화문을 발표하다'로 나와요. '담화'는 말로 하는 이야기도 포함하지만, 담화문은 글로 된 문서라는 점이 달라요.

phrases.en: The prime minister read the statement.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공식 입장을 글로 읽어 알릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when reading out an official written statement.

phrases.en: The address to the nation was broadcast.
phrases.nuance_ko: 국민 모두에게 전하는 공식 글을 말하고 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: An official text addressed to the whole nation, common in news.

phrases.en: The spokesperson announced a statement.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말로 하는 이야기도 포함해서 담화문보다 넓게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Broader than 담화문, including spoken statements.

explain_en: It refers to a written text issued by a government or organization to announce its official position, and mostly appears in the news as '담화문을 발표하다'. '담화' can include spoken talk, but 담화문 is a written document.

examples.ko: 그는 낮에는 막노동자로 일하고 밤에는 공부해요.
examples.en: He works as a laborer by day and studies at night.
The laborers gathered at the site from early morning.
I watched a documentary about a day in the life of a laborer.
My father was a laborer, but I'm not ashamed.

examples.ko: 막노동자에게 따뜻한 국밥 한 그릇을 대접했어요.
examples.en: I treated the laborer to a bowl of warm soup with rice.
These days it's hard even to find laborers.

explain: 남을 가리킬 때는 '일용직 노동자'나 '현장 노동자'가 더 중립적이에요. 막노동자는 그대로 쓰면 낮춰 부르는 말로 들릴 수 있으니 조심해요. 자기 가족 이야기나 다큐·기사에서는 자연스럽게 나와요.

phrases.en: Day laborers gathered early in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남을 말할 때는 이 말이 더 중립적이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more neutral term when referring to others.

phrases.en: The safety of site workers is the most important thing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공사장 같은 곳에서 일하는 사람을 존중해서 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A respectful term for people working at sites like construction.

phrases.en: That writer used to be a laborer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기사나 이야기에서 지난 직업을 말할 때 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Natural in articles or stories when describing a past job.

explain_en: Sino-Korean compound for a worker doing unskilled manual labor (막노동); more neutral, suits writing. When referring to others, '일용직 노동자' or '현장 노동자' is more neutral. 막노동자 used bluntly can sound demeaning, so be careful. It appears naturally in stories about one's own family and in documentaries or articles.

t90.ax: These days it's hard even to find laborers.

examples.en: That restaurant is doing booming business every lunchtime.

examples.ko: 골목 안 그 빵집은 요즘 완전히 성업이에요.
examples.en: The bakery in that alley is thriving these days.

examples.ko: 새로 연 카페가 성업을 이루고 있어요.
examples.en: The newly opened cafe is doing thriving business.

examples.ko: 성업 중인 가게 앞에는 줄이 길어요.
examples.en: There is a long line in front of the busy shop.

examples.ko: 성업 덕분에 사장님이 직원을 더 뽑았어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the booming business, the owner hired more staff.

examples.ko: 손님이 끊이지 않으니 성업이라고 할 만해요.
examples.en: Customers keep coming, so you can call it a thriving business.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '장사가 잘되다'라고 말하고, '성업'은 뉴스나 가게 소개 글에서 '성업 중'으로 많이 나와요. 가게나 사업이 번창할 때 쓰고 사람에게는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.example: 성업 중인 식당이 이 골목에 많아요.
phrases.en: There are many thriving restaurants on this street.
phrases.nuance_ko: '성업 중' 뒤에 '-인'을 붙여 명사를 꾸밀 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-인' after 성업 중 lets it modify a noun.

phrases.en: Business is good on this street.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '성업'을 쉽게 바꿔 말한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The everyday, easy way to say what 성업 means.

phrases.en: The newly opened shop is thriving these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게나 사업이 점점 커지고 잘될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a shop or business keeps growing and doing well.

explain_en: Business doing well with many customers (성업 중) In daily conversation people say '장사가 잘되다', while '성업' mostly shows up in news and shop descriptions as '성업 중'. It is used for shops and businesses that prosper, not for people.

examples.ko: 공사장에서 인부 열 명이 일하고 있어요.
examples.en: Ten laborers are working at the construction site.
The workers rested in the shade during lunch.
I saved up my tuition by working as a laborer.
The construction is delayed because there aren't enough workers.

examples.ko: 이삿짐 인부들은 정말 빠르고 힘이 세요.
examples.en: The moving workers are really fast and strong.

examples.ko: 인부를 구하는 광고가 전봇대에 붙어 있었어요.
examples.en: An ad looking for laborers was stuck on the utility pole.

explain: '노동자'나 '근로자'는 일하는 사람 모두를 부르지만, 인부는 공사·이사처럼 몸으로 하는 일을 하는 사람에게 주로 써서 조금 낮춰 부르는 느낌이 있어요. 직접 부를 때는 '아저씨'나 '선생님'이 더 정중해요.

phrases.en: The construction site workers start working early in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인부가 일하는 곳을 붙여서 가장 흔하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to use it, naming the place where they work.

phrases.en: I'm looking for workers for the move.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일할 사람을 찾을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used when looking for people to hire for physical work.

phrases.en: The workers on the construction site wear helmets.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인부보다 공식적이고 낮춰 보는 느낌이 없어서 글에서 더 안전해요.
phrases.nuance_en: More formal and without the slightly looking-down feel of 인부, so it is safer in writing.

explain_en: Physical laborer at work sites like construction. '노동자' and '근로자' cover anyone who works, while 인부 is mainly for people doing physical work such as construction or moving, and it can sound slightly condescending. When addressing such a person directly, '아저씨' or '선생님' is more polite.

t90.ax: The workers rested in the shade during lunch.

en: to gather news materials; to cover

examples.en: A reporter covers the accident scene.
Our newspaper covered that incident.
I went at dawn to interview the people at the market.
I only write articles from what I've reported myself.
I'm going to cover the players tomorrow.
I heard many stories while reporting.

explain: 기자나 방송 작가가 기사를 쓰려고 현장에 가서 사람을 만나고 자료를 모을 때만 써요. 일반인이 정보를 찾을 때는 '조사하다'나 '알아보다'를 쓰고, 취재하다를 쓰면 기자가 된 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: The reporter went out to the scene to gather material.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기자가 밖으로 일하러 갈 때 쓰는 자연스러운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A natural phrase for a reporter heading out on assignment.

phrases.en: The press gathered at the accident scene.
phrases.nuance_ko: 취재하는 기자들을 한꺼번에 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A group term for the reporters covering a story.

phrases.en: The reporter is covering a story at the market right now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 일하는 중이라는 뜻으로, 뉴스에서 자주 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means working on it right now; common in news.

explain_en: It is used only when a journalist or broadcast writer goes to a scene, meets people, and gathers material for a story. Ordinary people looking things up say '조사하다' or '알아보다'; using 취재하다 makes you sound like a reporter.

examples.ko: 밤늦게 고성방가를 하면 이웃에게 피해를 줘요.
examples.en: If you sing and shout loudly late at night, you disturb your neighbors.

examples.ko: 공원에서 고성방가 하는 사람들 때문에 시끄러워요.
examples.en: It is noisy because of people singing and shouting in the park.

examples.ko: 고성방가는 다른 사람에게 방해가 되니까 조심하세요.
examples.en: Loud singing and shouting bothers other people, so please be careful.

examples.ko: 옆집에서 고성방가 소리가 들려서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: I heard loud singing from next door and couldn't sleep.
There is a sign saying loud singing and shouting is banned on the beach.

examples.ko: 늦은 밤 고성방가로 신고를 받았다고 해요.
examples.en: I heard they got a report about loud shouting late at night.

explain: 주로 '고성방가를 하다', '고성방가를 금지하다'처럼 안내판이나 뉴스, 신고 이야기에서 나와요. 평소 말로는 '시끄럽게 떠들다', '소리 지르며 노래하다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 술에 취한 사람이 길에서 고성방가를 했어요.
phrases.en: A drunk person was loudly singing in the street.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신고나 뉴스에서 자주 나오는 기본 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic phrase seen in reports and news.

phrases.en: Loud singing and shouting are banned in this park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내판이나 규칙에 쓰는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Wording used on signs and rules.

phrases.en: Please don't make loud noise at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 평소 대화에서는 이 말이 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural in everyday conversation.

explain_en: It mostly appears in phrases like '고성방가를 하다' or '고성방가를 금지하다' on signs, in the news, or in noise reports. In casual speech people say '시끄럽게 떠들다' instead.

examples.ko: 요즘 막장 드라마를 매일 챙겨 봐요.
examples.en: These days I watch an over-the-top soap opera every day.

examples.ko: 이 드라마는 내용이 너무 막장이라서 웃음이 나요.
examples.en: The plot of this drama is so outrageous that it makes me laugh.

examples.ko: 막장 전개인 걸 알면서도 계속 보게 돼요.
examples.en: I keep watching even though I know the plot is over the top.

examples.ko: 남편이 갑자기 사라지는 막장 설정에 다들 놀랐어요.
examples.en: Everyone was shocked by the outrageous setup where the husband suddenly vanishes.
Something totally crazy happened at the company.

examples.ko: 광부들이 막장에서 일하는 모습을 사진으로 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a photo of miners working at the end of the mine tunnel.

explain: 원래는 광산에서 갱도의 맨 끝을 가리키는 말이에요. 지금은 드라마가 현실에서 있을 수 없는 자극적인 이야기로 흘러갈 때 '막장 드라마'라고 해요. 조금 비웃거나 비꼬는 느낌이 있어서 좋은 평가는 아니에요.

phrases.example: 그 막장 드라마는 매주 새로운 사건이 생겨요.
phrases.en: That over-the-top drama has a new incident every week.
phrases.nuance_ko: '막장'이 가장 흔히 붙는 말이에요. 현실에서 있을 수 없는 자극적인 이야기의 드라마를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing; it refers to a drama with sensational, unrealistic stories.

phrases.en: The ending of this movie is really outrageous.
phrases.nuance_ko: '막장'을 서술어로 써서 이야기가 지나치다고 말할 때 써요. 조금 비꼬는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Using it as a predicate to say a story goes too far; it has a slightly sarcastic tone.

phrases.en: The story is getting more and more outrageous.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이야기가 점점 이상하고 자극적으로 변할 때 써요. 보통 불만을 말할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a story gradually turns weird and sensational, usually as a complaint.

explain_en: Originally it is the very end of a mine tunnel. Now '막장 드라마' is a drama whose story goes into shocking, unrealistic territory. It has a mocking tone, so it is not praise.

en: to be broadcast; to be aired

examples.en: That drama airs every Saturday.
I watched the program that aired yesterday.

examples.ko: 새 예능이 다음 달부터 방영될 거예요.
examples.en: The new variety show will start airing next month.
This film was not aired in Korea.
That drama became popular as soon as it aired.

examples.ko: 오래전에 방영됐던 만화를 다시 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to watch the cartoon that aired a long time ago again.

explain: '방영되다'는 TV로 드라마, 영화, 만화 같은 영상이 나올 때 써요. 라디오나 뉴스까지 넓게 말할 때는 '방송되다'를 써요. 방송국 쪽이 주어면 '방영하다', 프로그램이 주어면 '방영되다'예요.

phrases.en: That drama is currently airing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 TV에서 나오고 있다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it is currently being shown on TV.

phrases.en: The broadcaster will air the new drama starting tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방송국이 주어일 때는 '방영하다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 방영하다 when the broadcaster is the subject.

phrases.example: 이 프로그램은 밤 열 시에 방송돼요.
phrases.en: This program is broadcast at ten at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 라디오나 뉴스까지 넓게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broader word that also covers radio and news.

explain_en: Passive, TV dramas and programs shown on a schedule; narrower, written tone. 방영되다 is used when a video program such as a drama, film, or cartoon is shown on TV. For a broader sense that includes radio and news, Koreans use 방송되다. When the broadcaster is the subject it is 방영하다, and when the program is the subject it is 방영되다.

gh: aired on TV or radio, any content

p.n: 방송되다 is the general word; 방영되다 stresses that the program itself is being aired.

en: TV at home; the home TV audience

examples.en: This drama has captivated TV viewers at home for the first time in a while.
A new historical drama has come to TV screens at home.
Every weekend, TV at home is filled with family dramas.
That actor has returned to TV dramas and is the talk of the town.
There were many tear-jerking scenes on TV at home.

examples.ko: 스트리밍 서비스 때문에 안방극장도 변하고 있어요.
examples.en: Because of streaming services, TV drama at home is changing too.

explain: 집에서 TV로 보는 드라마나 방송을 극장에 빗댄 말이에요. 주로 뉴스 기사나 방송 소개 글에서 쓰고, 대화에서는 그냥 '드라마'라고 해요. '안방극장을 사로잡다', '안방극장에 돌아오다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: This drama captivated TV viewers at home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기사에서 드라마가 큰 인기를 얻었다는 뜻으로 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Most common in articles to say a drama became hugely popular.

phrases.en: The actor has returned to TV after a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오랜만에 TV 드라마에 다시 나온다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means appearing in a TV drama again after a long time.

phrases.example: 안방극장의 인기 드라마는 매주 화제가 돼요.
phrases.en: Popular TV dramas become a hot topic every week.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의'를 붙여 안방극장에서 인기를 끈다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 'ui' to say something is popular on home TV.

explain_en: It compares watching dramas and shows on TV at home to a theater. It is used mainly in news articles and show introductions, while in conversation people just say '드라마'. It appears in phrases like '안방극장을 사로잡다' and '안방극장에 돌아오다'.

examples.en: The world these days is truly a bewildering mess.

examples.ko: 요지경 같은 세상에서 살려면 마음이 단단해야 해요.
examples.en: To live in a world this bewildering, you need a strong heart.

examples.ko: 이 드라마는 요지경 세상을 재미있게 그렸어요.
examples.en: This drama portrays the topsy-turvy world in an entertaining way.

examples.ko: 요즘 우리 회사 일이 요지경이라 이해가 안 돼요.
examples.en: Things at my company are such a muddle these days that I can't make sense of them.

examples.ko: 할머니는 어릴 때 구경한 요지경 이야기를 해 주셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother told me about a peep show she watched as a child.

examples.ko: 세상이 요지경 속이라서 누구를 믿어야 할지 모르겠어요.
examples.en: The world is such a muddle that I don't know whom to trust.

explain: 작은 구멍으로 들여다보는 구경거리를 뜻하지만, 요즘에는 '세상은 요지경이다'처럼 복잡하고 알 수 없는 세상을 비유할 때 훨씬 많이 써요. 어이없는 일이 많다는 가벼운 푸념에 어울려요.

phrases.example: 요지경 속 같은 연예계 소식에 모두 놀랐어요.
phrases.en: Everyone was shocked by the bewildering news from the entertainment world.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세상이나 일이 복잡하고 알 수 없다는 뜻으로, 한숨 섞인 푸념에 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means a world or situation that is complicated and hard to figure out; often said with a sigh.

explain_en: It originally refers to a peep show viewed through a small hole, but today it is used far more as a metaphor for a complicated, baffling world, as in '세상은 요지경이다'. It suits a light complaint about absurd things happening.

examples.en: I want to major in meteorology at university.
I learned the types of clouds in meteorology class.
Meteorologists are analyzing the typhoon's path.
Meteorology gets more interesting the more you study it.

examples.ko: 기상학에 관심이 생겨서 관련 책을 샀어요.
examples.en: I became interested in meteorology and bought a related book.

examples.ko: 기상학적으로 보면 올해 여름은 유난히 더웠어요.
examples.en: Meteorologically speaking, this summer was unusually hot.

explain: '기상 예보'의 '기상'은 날씨를 뜻하고, '기상 시간'의 '기상'은 잠에서 일어나는 것이라 서로 달라요. 일상에서는 '날씨'라고 쉽게 말하고, '기상학'은 수업이나 학문 이야기에서 나와요.

phrases.en: My uncle works as a meteorologist.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기상학을 연구하는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A person who studies meteorology.

phrases.example: 기상학을 공부하면 날씨를 더 잘 알 수 있어요.
phrases.en: If you study meteorology, you can understand the weather better.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학문으로 배운다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means learning it as an academic subject.

phrases.example: 기상학 연구 덕분에 태풍을 더 잘 예측해요.
phrases.en: Thanks to meteorology research, we predict typhoons better.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연구 결과를 이야기할 때 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears when talking about research results.

explain_en: The '기상' in '기상 예보' refers to weather, while the '기상' in '기상 시간' means waking up, so they are different words. In daily life people just say '날씨', and '기상학' appears in classes and academic talk.

examples.ko: 내일은 기압골의 영향으로 전국에 비가 와요.
examples.en: Tomorrow it will rain nationwide because of a pressure trough.
A pressure trough is approaching from the west.
Clouds spread widely along the pressure trough.

examples.ko: 일기예보에서 기압골 때문에 비가 온다고 했어요.
examples.en: The weather forecast said it will rain because of a pressure trough.

examples.ko: 기압골에 의해 제주도에 많은 눈이 내린대요.
examples.en: I heard heavy snow is falling on Jeju because of a pressure trough.
It thundered all night because of a pressure trough.

explain: 일기예보에서 '기압골의 영향으로 비가 오겠습니다'처럼 들리는 말이에요. 친구와 말할 때는 '비구름이 온대'처럼 쉽게 말해요.

phrases.example: 기압골의 영향으로 주말에 바람이 강하게 불어요.
phrases.en: Because of the pressure trough, the wind blows strongly on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일기예보에서 비나 바람의 원인을 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase in weather forecasts for explaining the cause of rain or wind.

phrases.en: A pressure trough is approaching from the west, so the sky has turned cloudy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 날씨가 곧 나빠질 것 같을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation used when the weather is about to get worse.

phrases.en: Once the pressure trough passes, the weather clears up again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비가 그치고 날씨가 좋아질 때 함께 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the rain stops and the weather improves.

explain_en: You hear it in weather forecasts, as in '기압골의 영향으로 비가 오겠습니다' (rain is expected due to a pressure trough). With friends, people say it simply, like '비구름이 온대' (rain clouds are coming).

examples.en: Agricultural water has become scarce because of the drought.
A reservoir plays the role of supplying water for farming.
Water used for farming is managed separately.

examples.ko: 이 강물은 농업용수에도 쓰이고 식수에도 쓰여요.
examples.en: This river water is used for both farming and drinking.

examples.ko: 비가 와서 농업용수 확보가 한결 쉬워졌어요.
examples.en: With the rain, securing farming water has become much easier.

examples.ko: 농업용수는 논에 물을 댈 때 가장 많이 필요해요.
examples.en: Farming water is needed most when irrigating rice paddies.

explain: 쓰임에 따라 물을 나눈 이름으로 '식수(마시는 물)', '공업용수'와 함께 알아 두면 좋아요. 논밭에 대는 물을 가리키고, 뉴스에서 가뭄 소식과 함께 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: It hasn't rained, so there isn't enough agricultural water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가뭄 소식에서 가장 자주 나오는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The phrase most often seen in drought news.

phrases.en: The reservoir supplies agricultural water to the village.
phrases.nuance_ko: 논밭에 물을 대 주는 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for supplying water to fields.

phrases.en: Factories use a lot of industrial water.
phrases.nuance_ko: '농업용수'와 함께 알아 두면 좋은, 공장에서 쓰는 물이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Good to learn alongside '농업용수'; it is water used in factories.

explain_en: It is one of the names that sort water by use, alongside '식수' (drinking water) and '공업용수' (industrial water). It refers to water for fields and paddies and often appears in news about droughts.

examples.ko: 이 호수는 겨울 철새 도래지로 유명해요.
examples.en: This lake is famous as a winter stop for migratory birds.
I went to a migratory bird site and saw cranes.
Please walk quietly near the bird sanctuary.

examples.ko: 개발 때문에 철새 도래지가 줄고 있어요.
examples.en: Migratory bird sites are shrinking because of development.
They restricted entry to protect the bird site.

examples.ko: 올겨울에는 도래지에 새가 많이 오지 않았어요.
examples.en: This winter, not many birds came to the site.

explain: 실제로는 주로 '철새 도래지'로 써요. 철새가 계절에 따라 날아와 머무는 곳을 말해요. 뉴스, 여행, 환경 이야기에서 자주 나오고, 새가 먹이를 찾아 쉬어 가는 호수나 갯벌을 가리킬 때가 많아요.

phrases.en: This tidal flat is a famous migratory bird site.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표제어가 거의 항상 이 짝말로 쓰이므로 가장 먼저 외우면 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word almost always appears in this pairing, so learn it first.

phrases.example: 이 섬은 겨울에 두루미 도래지로 유명해요.
phrases.en: This island is famous as a winter stopover for cranes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 곳이 새가 많이 오는 곳으로 알려져 있다고 소개할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to introduce a place known for the birds that come there.

phrases.example: 사진작가가 철새 도래지를 찾아 길을 떠났어요.
phrases.en: The photographer set out to find a migratory bird site.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새를 보러 가거나 조사하러 갈 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when going to watch or study the birds.
phrases.en_equiv: to look for an arrival site

explain_en: In practice it is mostly used as '철새 도래지', a place where migratory birds arrive and stay by season. It often appears in news, travel and environmental topics, usually for lakes or tidal flats where birds rest and feed.

examples.en: The heat wave is raging this summer.
The flu raged, so school was closed.
The market opened even amid the fierce cold wave.

examples.ko: 겨울 추위가 맹위를 떨칠 때는 집에 있고 싶어요.
examples.en: When winter cold rages, I want to stay home.

examples.ko: 새로운 바이러스가 맹위를 떨칠까 봐 걱정이에요.
examples.en: I'm worried a new virus might rage.
All the street trees fell to the fury of the typhoon.

explain: 거의 '맹위를 떨치다'라는 짝말로 쓰고, 더위, 추위, 태풍, 질병처럼 사람이 막기 어려운 힘이 강할 때 써요. 사람의 성격이나 기분에는 잘 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: The cold is raging fiercely this winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: '맹위를 떨치다'를 해요체로 말한 거예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite 해요체 form of '맹위를 떨치다'.

phrases.example: 맹위를 떨치는 태풍 때문에 비행기가 취소됐어요.
phrases.en: Flights were canceled because of the raging typhoon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞의 '맹위를 떨치는'이 뒤의 명사를 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: '맹위를 떨치는' describes the noun that follows.

phrases.en: The fierce heat that had been raging has finally ended.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 지나간 일을 말할 때는 '떨친'으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '떨친' when talking about something already past.

explain_en: It is almost always used in the set phrase '맹위를 떨치다', for forces hard to stop such as heat, cold, typhoons and diseases. It is not used for a person's character or mood.
